title: Cybercrime Group FIN7 Using Windows 11 Alpha- Themed Docs to Drop Javascript Backdoor

attributes.evidence_span: Related Groups FIN7 is closely associated with the threat group referred to as “Carbanak,” with the two groups sharing a significant number of TTPs including the use of the Carbanak backdoor.

evidences.text: anomali.com /blog/cybercrime-group-fin7-using-windows-11-alpha-themed-docs-to-drop-javascript-backdoor Authored by: Gage Mele, Tara Gould, Rory Gould, and Sean Townsend
Related Groups FIN7 is closely associated with the threat group referred to as “Carbanak,” with the two groups sharing a significant number of TTPs including the use of the Carbanak backdoor.
To add to the confusion, different vendors will use their own naming conventions for each group that include:
FIN7 - Carbon Spider (Crowdstrike), Gold Niagara (Secureworks), Calcium (Symantec) Carbanak - Carbon Spider (Crowdstrike), Anunak (Group-IB)
For clarity, we will treat FIN7 and Carbanak as separate groups; the main distinction being FIN7 focuses on hospitality and retail sectors, while Carbanak targets banking institutions.
Shown in Figure 9, the script checks for the domain CLEARMIND, which appears to refer to the domain of a Point-of-Sale (POS) service provider.

Domain name, specifically CLEARMIND (Figure 9) Language, if any of the languages listed in Table 1 Reg Key Language Preference for Russian Virtual machine - VMWare, VirtualBox, innotek, QEMU, Oracle, Hyper and Parallels, if a VM is detected the script is killed (Figure 8) Memory Available, if there is less than 4GB then don’t proceed Check for RootDSE via LDAP
If the checks are satisfactory, the script proceeds to the function where a JavaScript file called word_data.js is dropped to the TEMP folder.
Analyzing the XOR cipher function, ‘ben9qtdx4t’ is the key used to decrypt the strings in the JavaScript file (word_data.js).

A connection is first made to ‘tnskvggujjqfcskwk.com,’ (Figure 14) and based on the response, a connection is then made to ‘bypassociation[.]com.’ This address is created by picking values from each array (Figure 15) at random.

After connecting to the bypassociation[.]com address, the script checks for an active IP to retrieve the MAC address and DNSHostName (Figure 16), which are then submitted via a POST request to the bypassociation address.
Attribution The specified targeting of the Clearmind domain fits well with FIN7’s preferred modus operandi.

As a California-based provider of POS technology for the retail and hospitality sector, a successful infection would allow the group to obtain payment card data and later sell the information on online marketplaces.
The use of a JavaScript backdoor is also primarily associated with FIN7 and is a common feature within its campaigns.
It is worth noting that Carbanak has also been known to use Javascript payloads but, as this targets retail and health POS systems, it aligns with FIN7 activity.

The addition of Sorbian, a minority German Slavic language, Estonian, Slovenian and Slovak are unusual additions as these would not be languages considered for exclusion but would be considered ‘fair game.’ It is worth noting that REvil ransomware also includes these languages in their exclusion tables, a group that is believed to work with FIN7.
